claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000°C.
Spark plasma sintering at approximately 1300°C and 50 MPa for 5 minutes can produce 3–5 vol% sub-micrometer porosity in HfMoTaTiZr powder.
The proposed partial-sintering treatment will form a uniform, interconnected network of sub-micrometer pores.
The proposed pore network will decrease the bulk density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The pore network will not severely compromise grain-boundary integrity or phase continuity.
Well-sintered metallurgical bonds remaining after partial sintering will maintain load-transfer capability despite the porosity.
Maintained load transfer will preserve yield strength at both room temperature and 1000°C.
The SPS-treated alloy will have a density at least 3–5% below the as-cast value.
The SPS-treated alloy will have a density below 10.2 g/cm³.
The SPS-treated alloy's room-temperature yield strength will remain within 5% of approximately 1600 MPa.
The SPS-treated alloy's yield strength at 1000°C will remain within 5% of approximately 855 MPa.
Mechanical performance will be evaluated under quasi-static loading at approximately 25°C and 1000°C.
Pore volume fraction will be maintained between 3 and 5 vol% and determined by density measurements and microstructural analysis such as X-ray tomography.
Controlling pore size and distribution during SPS may affect ductility or toughness.
The long-term stability of the SPS-treated material under cyclic or oxidative conditions is not established.
An arc-cast HfMoTaTiZr control and an SPS-processed HfMoTaTiZr test group will be compared using density, tomography, microscopy, and mechanical testing.
The hypothesis is rejected if density is not below 10.2 g/cm³ or if yield strength at either test temperature decreases by more than 5% relative to the as-cast control.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 3–5% density reduction from 10.21 g/cm³, which implies roughly 9.70–9.90 g/cm³, but the rejection rule only requires density below 10.2 g/cm³. A much smaller reduction could therefore pass the falsification rule while failing the stated prediction.

The predicted outcome requires yield strengths within ±5% of baseline, whereas the falsification rule rejects only decreases greater than 5%. A strength increase greater than 5% would violate the stated ±5% prediction but would not falsify the hypothesis under the rejection rule.
